spec_match.rationale: Demonstrates exactly the spec's source-element breadth (a, form, submit input, button) and lifecycle (matches during the navigation, nothing after, nothing on traversal), with the per-trigger source semantics mirroring the css-navigation-1 WPT navigation-source-001.html expectations: click→link, submitter→button not form, form.submit()/requestSubmit()→form, requestSubmit(btn)→btn, traversal→none.

interactive.rationale: Six real navigation triggers (real link, real form submission, three programmatic submits, navigation.back()), each intercepted and held open, with a per-element results table and live mirror highlight.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card promises different sources per trigger including the traversal case; that is precisely the stage.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers traversal-has-no-source, submitter-vs-form distinction, back() with no earlier entry (guarded with a message), re-trigger while a navigation is held open (busy guard), selector-throws surfaced per row, and a disabled honest fallback when the Navigation API is missing.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/6327898878377984, the spec anchor, and the WHATWG sourceElement definition.

conformance.rationale: The feature-level suite covers the matching-API contracts this page relies on (matches doesn't throw, nothing matches at rest); suite executes on the conformance route without runner errors.

runtime_evidence.rationale: All six triggers exercised in headless Chromium 141 at 1280×800 and 360×740 via scripted Playwright over the real Chromium binary: link→a#link1, btn1 not form1, form2 via submit(), btn3 not form3, form4 via requestSubmit(), traversal→no sim class anywhere; mirror removed after navigatesuccess; keyboard Tab+Enter on the link fired the same flow. chrome-devtools-mcp unavailable in this environment, and the native solid-outline branch needs a ≥156 build.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts stage-armed, per-navigation navigation-sampled with type and source, traversal-has-no-source, and nav-api-missing-fallback-shown on the degraded branch.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout; the programmatic-button variant overrides background AND color together; table wrapped in an overflow-x scroller; dashed simulation legend uses accent-rose on bg-stone (AA for large bold text) with meaning also carried in table text.

accessibility.rationale: role=status aria-live output narrates every navigation and settle; results are a real table with scoped headers and text verdicts (colour is not the only channel); all triggers are native links/buttons ≥44px; the unsupported branch disables controls with an explanation instead of hiding them.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Zero page-level horizontal overflow at 360×740 DPR3 (scrollWidth 360; the results table scrolls inside its own container); candidate cards stack to one column; all six flows re-run and verified at the mobile viewport with identical results.

openQuestions.title: Observe the native solid-outline match on a Chrome 156+ build
openQuestions.detail: The page's stylesheet rule :navigation-source { outline: … } is in place and the per-row matches() column will flip from SyntaxError to yes/no on a supporting build, but this could not be observed on Chromium 141 (flag predates the build). Re-run the six triggers on Chrome Canary ≥156 and confirm the solid outline coincides with the dashed mirror and that the 'still matching after finish' warning never appears.

openQuestions.title: Confirm cross-document behaviour is out of scope or add a note
openQuestions.detail: All navigations here are intercepted into same-document navigations. The pseudo-class also matches during genuine cross-document navigations on the outgoing page; a supporting-build verification could add a short observed note (the thumbnail-to-hero page discusses this but neither can demonstrate it pre-156).

guidanceConsulted.query: styling in-progress navigations and cross-document view transitions
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use Navigation API interception for same-document state changes so navigations stay real and observable.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Every trigger is a real navigation intercepted via navigate/intercept with the handler holding the matching window open, rather than simulated class toggling on a timer.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible loading progress status announcements live region
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Surface async state changes through polite live regions and never rely on colour alone.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The status readout is role=status aria-live=polite; source/matching state is also written as table text per element, so the outline colours are redundant encoding.

summary: The breadth-and-lifecycle page: six real navigations, per-element JS truth vs native-selector probe, WPT-aligned source semantics verified interactively on Chromium 141 at both viewports with a clean console. Native matching remains to be observed on a ≥156 build.
